help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While a download is paused: If you choose another source for a file that had already started downloading, the choice is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown stay as they are, and next to the service name a message shows where the file will move to (for example Switching to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume). Choosing again replaces it, and choosing the source in use clears the message. When you resume, Switching to … is shown until the switch takes effect, and then disappears. If paused files in the download have different destinations, or the destination is unknown, no destination is shown. A file that has never started has nothing to carry over, so the new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service while paused also works as described above, but the download stays paused. A service that can take over the link in use takes over immediately (shown in the badge); a service that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing… and takes over only after resuming. These messages appear in Download Activity and on the download's row, and both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, so that it is ready to take over if needed. Also, when a download is switched to another service, it keeps the torrent it had already started as a backup instead of removing it. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits, and new downloads that need a slot take slots back with priority. To keep that service's slots for its own downloads, turn it off. In that case, that service's backups are removed. Selections already saved are kept.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each user's role, sign-in method and whether the account is enabled. Clicking an account's name shows its details and activity, where outstanding requests can be withdrawn individually. Disable and Remove first show the number of that account's outstanding download requests. Those requests are withdrawn, but transfers that others also requested continue as they are, and completed downloads are not affected at all. Disabling also ends that account's signed-in sessions and stops its tokens. Removing keeps the account's history and deletes the account's own notification settings. If a removed OIDC sign-in appears again, a new account is created and stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the one account you chose to keep. Two accounts with the same verified email address are pointed out, but they are merged only if you run the merge. DebridPulse always keeps at least one available administrator. Also, you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

help.trouble.i_cannot_sign.last_resort_i.backTranslation: Last resort (if no sign-in method works): This requires access to the computer running DebridPulse and temporarily removes all protection, so do it only on a trusted network. Stop DebridPulse and back up its settings file (usually {path} inside the container). In that file, set {literal_1} and {literal_2} to {literal_3}. Keep the file valid JSON; if the settings file is broken, DebridPulse will not start. When you start DebridPulse, it will be open to everyone who can reach DebridPulse, including the API. Stored passwords and OIDC settings are kept, so repair them in "Settings → Authentication" and turn protection back on immediately.

help.trouble.backup_restore_reset.if_saf.backTranslation: If the safety backup fails, the reset or restore is aborted. Fix the Backup folder (location, permissions, free space). The safety backup cannot be skipped.

help.trouble.backup_restore_reset.if_res.backTranslation: If a restore could neither be completed nor rolled back (for example, the disk stopped accepting changes partway through), DebridPulse stops using its stored data. It answers every page and request saying a restart is required, and the health check reports unhealthy. The previous database and settings are kept. When the disk is writable again, restart the DebridPulse container yourself. On startup, the previous state is restored. Docker does not automatically restart the container even if the health check shows unhealthy.

help.quickstart.follow_finish.download_a.backTranslation: The download appears in the Dashboard's Download activity and in Downloads. help.notifications.how_saving_works.ther.backTranslation: There is no Save button. Each setting is saved individually. Typed values are saved when you move out of the field, and switch and list choices are saved as soon as you change them. If a value cannot be saved, a message explaining why is shown and the field returns to the saved value. A saved webhook is never shown again. Leaving the field blank keeps the saved webhook, and pressing Clear erases it.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Submitting a job creates a download request belonging to that application. Removing the job in the application withdraws that request; if delivery has completed, it acknowledges receipt of the delivery. The transfer itself stops only if no one else needs that transfer.
Completed files are shared in place. Files are never copied, linked or moved for the application, and files are never deleted because of a delivery acknowledgement or expiry.

help.topic.deployment_type.standalone.wi.backTranslation: If there is no password, no sign-in is needed, and DebridPulse is used as the built-in Administrator.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their username, password, identity provider link and saved Enabled or Disabled state. In Standalone, these accounts cannot sign in regardless of that state.
Switching clears the built-in Administrator's password, turns off sign-in by "Username and password" and OpenID Connect, and ends all browser sessions.

Afterwards, sign-in is no longer required. Anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address DebridPulse accepts can use DebridPulse as the built-in administrator. This is not limited to this computer and has no time limit.
